candidates.title: Epoch listener starts fetching InputAdded logs at the previous seal's block, so inputs left pending by the 2^24 per-epoch limit (or logged before the consensus deployment block) are never delivered and the honest player aborts
candidates.component: doc/recipes PRT player process and epoch listener (crisium.lua, prt-epoch.lua)
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an operator; stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua open_epochs(), lines 228-270 (input_begin = previous_seal.inputIndexUpperBound, first_input_block = previous_seal.log.blockNumber or first_block); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua methods:poll(), lines 37 and 72-76 (assert 'input stream has a gap or duplicate') and 94-97 (assert 'sealed input count mismatch'); referee side: DaveConsensus.sol _nextInputIndexUpperBound() and constructor (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol)
candidates.description: DaveConsensus seals epoch N with inputs [lower, lower + min(pending, 2^24)) and 'excess inputs stay pending' for epoch N+1. Those excess inputs were logged by the InputBox BEFORE the block of EpochSealed(N). The recipe's listener for epoch N correctly skips them (comment: 'an input after the seal, or past the epoch's input limit, belongs to a later player'), but crisium opens the listener of epoch N+1 with input_begin = seal(N).inputIndexUpperBound and first_input_block = the block of seal(N) (comment: 'An input logged in the previous seal's block can still belong to this epoch'). The listener therefore never fetches the backlog inputs logged in earlier blocks. The first InputAdded it sees has an index above input_begin and trips assert(index == self.input_begin + #self.inputs, 'input stream has a gap or duplicate'); if no later input arrives, EpochSealed(N+1) trips 'sealed input count mismatch'. The process exits, the supervisor relaunches it, and it fails the same way forever, so the honest player never computes or posts the claim of epoch N+1. The same root cause hits epoch 0 of a DaveConsensus created for an application that already has inputs (the constructor seals _nextInputIndexUpperBound(0) pending inputs into epoch 0, but the listener of epoch 0 starts at getDeploymentBlockNumber()).
candidates.trigger: An input sender. Variant A: sends more than 2^24 inputs to the application between two consecutive EpochSealed events (about 60k gas per minimal addInput, about 1e12 gas in total; epochs last at least the tournament's lifetime, so the inputs can be spread over days), with input number lower+2^24 logged in a block before the seal. Variant B (deployment where the consensus is not created atomically with the application): sends one input to the application in a block before the DaveConsensus deployment block.
candidates.reachability: On the honest operator's path (observing the chain, delivering inputs). Variant A needs only valid addInput transactions that the pinned InputBox accepts; the contract itself documents the case ('excess inputs stay pending', prt-lua-bridge.md: 'Its consensus seals at most 2^24 pending inputs per epoch and leaves the rest for later epochs'). Cost is high on L1 and low on a cheap chain. Variant B needs a deployment path other than DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp (which creates application and consensus in one transaction), e.g. an application migrated to a new DaveConsensus.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. The trigger is inputs the deployment accepts: section 7 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'. No reorg, no API misuse, no violated A1-A8 (A3 is honoured by the referee: 'The input record assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch').
rating_steps.2_role: AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.' Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: Matches the Medium case 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'. No unreachable-state argument is needed: the state is reached by plain inputs.
rating_steps.4_critical: In the honest-operator role it would be Critical: R4 'The honest operator defends every epoch whose dispute is open, including while it processes the inputs of later epochs. It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3).' and section 1 'Completeness failure. The honest operator computes a wrong hash, cannot produce a proof that verifies, or cannot respond in time.'
rating_steps.5_low: Not Low: a rule (R4) is violated on the honest operator's path of the operator implementation.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; Critical in the honest-operator role it stands in for)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness: once the backlog case occurs the honest player can never claim epoch N+1 (it aborts before sealing its player), so any claim posted by an adversary wins that epoch's tournament unopposed and a fabricated final state and outputs root can settle.
candidates.evidence: Ran the real prt-epoch.lua listener against a fake chain with the per-epoch limit lowered through the Lua constant it reads at load (cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH = 2, model of 24): six inputs logged in blocks 11-16, seal(N) = [0,4) at block 20, seal(N+1) = [4,6) at block 30, listener for N+1 created exactly as crisium does (input_begin = 4, first_input_block = 20). Result: 'poll ok: false error: prt-epoch.lua:96: sealed input count mismatch inputs delivered: 0' (two inputs should have been delivered). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERINPUT/t/backlog.lua. The referee side was read, not run: DaveConsensus._nextInputIndexUpperBound returns lowerBound + min(pending, 1 << ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH) and acceptStagedTournamentResult uses it for the next epoch.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test that requires prt-epoch with a fake chain object (head/is_canonical/logs) and fake ABI, lowers cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH before the require (or uses 2^24+1 synthetic logs), builds the log history that DaveConsensus would emit with MAX+k inputs pending at seal(N), opens the listener of epoch N+1 with the arguments crisium computes from seal(N), and asserts that poll() delivers inputs upper_N .. upper_N+k-1 to the player and seals it with k inputs. On audit/prt2 poll() raises instead (exit 1). A variant asserts the same for epoch 0 with one input logged before the consensus deployment block.

candidates.title: Open-epoch listener re-sorts and re-validates every log of the epoch on every pass (with big-integer conversions in the comparator); an input flood makes each pass exceed the block time, delays the sealed epoch's dispute ticks and starves input execution
candidates.component: doc/recipes PRT epoch listener and player main loop (prt-epoch.lua, crisium.lua)
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an operator; stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua methods:poll() lines 26-71 (rebuilds 'logs' from the whole history, table.sort(logs, less) where less() calls eth.small four times per comparison, then a loop computing key(log) and comparing with self.applied for every log), lines 77-83 (self.inputs keeps every input's bytes while the history keeps their hex and the stored player keeps a third copy on disk); doc/recipes/crisium.lua pass() lines 293-303 (every listener polls before any dispute bridge ticks) and main loop lines 368-392 (idle(), which runs pending inputs of the stored player, is called only when the tip did not change during the pass)
candidates.description: While an epoch is open, every pass (one per new block, plus retries) calls listener:poll(), which does work proportional to n log n in the number n of logs of the open epoch even when nothing new arrived: it copies all logs, converts blockNumber/logIndex with evmu.bint inside the sort comparator, and rebuilds an identity string per log. The cost per pass is therefore not bounded per input and the total over an epoch grows with (blocks x inputs). The pass of the open epoch runs before the tick of the sealed epoch's dispute bridge, so every response of the honest claim in the running dispute is delayed by it. Once a pass lasts longer than the block interval, the main loop finds a new tip after every pass and never reaches idle(), which is the only place the stored (honest) player executes pending inputs; the whole backlog is then executed synchronously inside epoch_sealed, on the joining clock of the new tournament. The listener also holds every input of the epoch in RAM twice (hex in the log history, raw in self.inputs) in addition to the stored copy.
candidates.trigger: An input sender who adds many small inputs to the application while an epoch is open (about 60k gas each). Measured: 20,000 inputs make each idle poll cost about 4.8 s, 80,000 inputs about 25 s (more than a 12 s block), with a trivial fake ABI decoder; real logs cost more.
candidates.reachability: On the honest operator's path (observing the chain). 80,000 minimal inputs are about 5e9 gas, far below the 2^24 inputs per epoch the deployment accepts; the cost scales super-linearly up to that limit (extrapolated: minutes per pass at 1e6 inputs, hours at 2^24).

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. Section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts, with payloads chosen to maximize the honest operator's cost (R12)'. The exclusion 'Average-case performance that does not change the worst-case cost of any operation listed in R12' does not apply: this is the worst-case cost of observing the chain.
rating_steps.2_role: Support (AUDIT.md component table: the PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes). Section 3: Medium 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'.
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: Medium case 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'. In the stood-in role it is not the High constant-factor case, because the cost is super-linear: 'When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High and a super-linear or unbounded one Critical.'
rating_steps.4_critical: In the honest-operator role: R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records, and restarting, has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match, and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open.' Here the cost per input grows with the number of blocks and of other inputs. Also A7/R4: 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and 'defends every epoch whose dispute is open, including while it processes the inputs of later epochs'.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; Critical in the honest-operator role by R12, super-linear cost)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness by timeout: a flood of cheap inputs into the open epoch slows every response of the honest claim in the dispute of the sealed epoch and keeps the player from executing the open epoch's inputs before its seal, so the honest claim can run out of clock or miss the joining window of the next tournament.
candidates.evidence: Benchmark of the real prt-epoch.lua with a fake chain (100 inputs per block, trivial ABI decoder): N=5000: idle poll 0.91 s; N=20000: 4.83 s; N=80000: 25.4 s, on every poll with no new log. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERINPUT/t/bench_poll.lua. The starvation of idle() and the ordering of polls before ticks were read from crisium.lua, not run.
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic test with a fake chain that counts work instead of time: wrap eth.small (or count comparator calls through a debug hook) and assert that a poll that observes no new log performs O(1) (or at most O(new logs)) conversions when the listener already applied N logs; on audit/prt2 the count grows as N log N (for example more than 4*N for N = 2000). A second assertion: after applying N inputs the listener does not keep N raw inputs plus N hex logs in memory.

candidates.title: Dispute bridge fetches, keeps and re-processes every log of the shared tournament factory since the epoch seal; factory.instantiate is permissionless, so chain activity unrelated to the application raises the honest player's cost and memory per observation
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an operator; stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:observe() lines 57-68 (addresses = { self.factory, self.consensus, self.root }, all fetched from first_block = seal block to the head without topics) and 106-121 (all logs sorted and scanned on every observation); doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua (logs retained per address); referee side: MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate() emits TournamentCreated with no indexed argument and ITournamentFactory.sol states 'Anyone can call instantiate'
candidates.description: The bridge needs one factory event, the TournamentCreated of its root, which is emitted in the seal transaction. It nevertheless fetches all logs of the factory from the seal block to the observed head on every observation, keeps them for the life of the epoch, and sorts and scans them again each time (a tick observes two or three times). The factory is shared by every application that uses it, and anyone can call instantiate() directly, so its log stream is chain activity that does not belong to the application. The per-observation time and the memory of the honest player grow linearly (n log n for the sort) with that activity.
candidates.trigger: Any account that calls MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate (or creates applications that share the factory) while the victim's epoch is in dispute. This is outside the strict input-sender persona (it is not an addInput), but inside section 7: 'Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application'. Inputs to other applications in the shared InputBox are NOT a trigger: the listener filters InputAdded by the indexed application topic.
candidates.reachability: On the honest operator's path (observing the chain) during any dispute. Each unrelated event costs the sender one instantiate call (a clone plus a log).

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded: no API misuse, no violated deployment obligation; the factory is used as deployed.
rating_steps.2_role: Support (AUDIT.md component table). Section 3 Medium rule for implementations of an operator.
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: Medium case 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'.
rating_steps.4_critical: In the honest-operator role: R12 'That total must not grow with the application's age, with the number of past epochs, or with chain activity that does not belong to the application.'
rating_steps.5_low: Not Low by the letter of R12; the practical magnitude is modest (see evidence), which a triager may weigh.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; R12 violation in the role it stands in for). Alternative reading: Low if triage treats the growth as too small to matter, since the per-log constant is small.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Erodes the clock margin of the honest claim: every observation of the dispute costs time and memory proportional to unrelated factory activity, so a third party can slow the honest player's responses or exhaust its memory without touching the application.
candidates.evidence: Benchmark of the real prt-bridge.lua observer with a fake chain and N unrelated TournamentCreated logs after the seal: N=20,000: 0.26 s per observation, 32 MB; N=200,000: 2.96 s per observation with no new log, 509 MB (small synthetic logs; real logs and the real ABI decoder cost more). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERINPUT/t/bench_factory.lua.
candidates.test_idea: With a fake chain, give the bridge a root created in the seal block and N later TournamentCreated logs of the same factory for other tournaments; assert that the observation snapshot (snapshot.logs) and the history do not retain them, or that the number of logs requested from the factory after the seal block is zero. On audit/prt2 snapshot.logs holds N+2 entries.

candidates.title: Player restart re-fetches and re-decodes the consensus log history from the deployment block (get_seal), so restart cost grows with the application's age and number of past epochs
candidates.component: doc/recipes PRT player process (crisium.lua get_seal/open_epochs, prt-log-history.lua paging)
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an operator; stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua lines 207-221 (seal_history = log_history.new(chain); get_seal(number) observes at the tip, calls seal_history:get_logs(consensus, first_block) with first_block = getDeploymentBlockNumber(), and decodes every log from the oldest until it finds the wanted EpochSealed), line 230 (called for the previous epoch of every listener it opens); doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua fetch() lines 76-108 (first page is the whole range, halved on failure and doubled on success)
candidates.description: To open the listener of epoch E the process needs seal(E-1). get_seal fetches all logs of the consensus from its deployment block to the tip, keeps them all in memory for the life of the process, and on every call decodes them again from the oldest one. After a restart the fetch covers the whole chain range since deployment; with a provider that limits the block range of eth_getLogs, the paging settles at about two requests per allowed range (a doubled page fails, the halved one succeeds). The time to restart, before the player can poll any epoch or tick any dispute, therefore grows linearly with the age of the application, and the decode work grows with the number of past epochs (EpochSealed, EpochStaged, SentryClaim logs).
candidates.trigger: No adversary action is needed beyond time passing; an input sender or claimant only has to wait for (or cause) a restart of the honest player during a dispute of an old application.
candidates.reachability: On the honest operator's path: 'Restarting after a stop (O2)'. Every start of crisium with a first epoch greater than zero runs it.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. The restart is from a guaranteed directory (O2); nothing else is assumed.
rating_steps.2_role: Support (AUDIT.md component table); section 3 Medium rule for implementations of an operator.
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: Medium case 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'.
rating_steps.4_critical: In the honest-operator role: R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records, and restarting, has a bounded cost ... That total must not grow with the application's age, with the number of past epochs, or with chain activity that does not belong to the application.' and R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim.'
rating_steps.5_low: Not Low by the letter of R12.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; R12 violation in the role it stands in for). Alternative reading: Low if the linear growth is judged harmless at realistic ages on slow chains.
candidates.threat_to_goal: A restarted honest player of a long-lived application (in particular on a chain with short block times) spends time proportional to the chain length since deployment before it resumes defending, which is clock taken from the honest claim.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (not run): crisium.lua get_seal and open_epochs; prt-log-history.lua fetch paging. Listeners and bridges themselves start at the previous seal's block, so only get_seal has this dependence.
candidates.test_idea: With a fake chain whose logs() rejects ranges longer than L blocks and counts requests, start the open_epochs logic (or a factored get_seal) for epoch E with the consensus deployed D blocks ago and seal(E-1) in the last L blocks; assert that the number of eth_getLogs requests and of decoded logs is bounded independently of D and of E. On audit/prt2 both grow linearly with D and E.

candidates.title: rollup --utf8-payload accept/reject/finish consumes the next advance request and then fails (exit 1, empty output) when its payload is not valid UTF-8
candidates.location: sys-utils/rollup/rollup.cpp: finish_request_and_get_next() and write_advance_state() (cmt_rollup_finish yields and receives the next request, then nlohmann::json::dump(2) throws type_error.316 on the payload string; the catch prints to stderr and returns 1); encode_payload() utf8 branch; help text of --utf8-payload; manual doc/README.md 'A simple calculator guest application' (calc.sh uses rollup --utf8-payload for requests)
candidates.description: In --utf8-payload mode the tool copies the payload bytes into a JSON string. For a payload that is not valid UTF-8 the JSON serializer throws after the accept/reject yield has already returned with the new request, so the request is consumed from the device, nothing is printed on stdout and the exit status is 1. The application cannot read that request again: its next accept acknowledges an input it never saw, and its next reject rejects it. The option's help ('encode/decode <data> fields in JSON values as UTF-8 text') does not say that a request with other bytes is lost.
candidates.trigger: An input sender: any input whose payload contains a byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 (for example the single byte 0xFF), sent to an application that reads its requests with rollup --utf8-payload.
candidates.reachability: Any such application, on every such input. The manual's calc.sh is such an application; it happens to end in a rejection because its status defaults to reject when the pipeline fails (verified), so it does not deviate.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Section 8 excludes 'Guest software that an input can subvert, as long as R7 and R8 hold, other than the defects that section 3 puts in scope'. Section 3 puts in scope a defect 'only where an application depends on them as documented, and would be correctly designed if they worked as documented'. An application that reads requests with the documented --utf8-payload option depends on it as documented.
rating_steps.2_role: Guest software (AUDIT.md: machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1). Section 3: 'A defect that lets an input make such an application deviate from the rollup interface is Critical, as an R7 deviation in the rx buffer, the tx buffer and the yield interface. Any other defect in them is Low.'
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: None of the listed High or Medium cases applies.
rating_steps.4_critical: Two readings. (a) The application still yields accepted or rejected with a consistent outputs root (as calc.sh does), so the rollup interface is followed and only the application's own result is wrong: not Critical. (b) An application that treats a failing tool as fatal (for example a script with set -e, or one that exits when the request cannot be parsed) halts on one such input instead of yielding, and it would be correctly designed if the tool returned every request as its help describes: that is an input-caused deviation, Critical by the quoted sentence. Which facts decide: whether failing on non-UTF-8 payloads counts as documented behavior of --utf8-payload, and whether losing the consumed request is part of 'the rx buffer ... (contents, lengths)'.
rating_steps.5_low: Under reading (a) it is 'Any other defect in them is Low'.

candidates.claimed_severity: Low (guest software); Critical under reading (b) above
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not threaten the honest operator. It lets an input make a shell application that uses the tool as documented lose that input's content, and, depending on how the script handles the failure, halt for good; the manual's own example survives only through its default-reject pattern.
candidates.evidence: Ran the in-tree emulator with the guest-tools rootfs: input payload '2+2 \xff\xfe\n'; command 'rollup --utf8-payload accept > /tmp/req; echo rc=$? size=$(wc -c < /tmp/req); rollup --hex-payload accept'. Output: '[json.exception.type_error.316] invalid UTF-8 byte at index 4: 0xFF', 'rc=1 size=0', then 'Manual yield rx-accepted': the second accept acknowledged the unread input. Running doc/recipes/calc.sh with inputs '2+2', '3+3 \xff', '4+4' gave a notice for the first and 'Manual yield rx-rejected' for the second. For comparison, ioctl-echo-loop and rollup-http-server (curl dapp) handled payload sizes 0, 1, 31, 32, 33, 64, 4095, 4096 and 65216 (random and all-zero bytes) with the CLI's outputs-Merkle-root check passing.
candidates.test_idea: bugs test.sh on the Linux template: deliver one advance input with payload byte 0xFF to a guest command that runs 'rollup --utf8-payload accept' and prints its exit status and output size; assert that the tool either exits 0 with a JSON request on stdout (payload escaped or replaced) or fails before consuming the request. On v0.18.1-test1 it exits 1 with empty output after the request was consumed.

not_covered: Emulator interpreter, uarch and device behavior driven by guest code after it reads an input (left to the rule-based angles); I only read input delivery (send-cmio-response.cpp, record/replay accessors, machine::send_cmio_response/log/verify, the Lua/C/JSON-RPC length checks) and found nothing to report.

Gas and transaction size of a winLeafMatch delivery proof for a maximum-size (64 KiB) InputBox input against real per-transaction limits: reasoned from the source (input in calldata, one Merkle root over 2048 leaves in provideMerkleRootOfInput), not measured on the chain harness.
The backlog case of candidate 1 on a real chain with the pinned DaveConsensus (2^24 inputs are infeasible on the local chain); the referee side was read only.

Differential comparison of computation hashes between the cartesi-machine CLI, the PRT player and the on-chain verifier for epochs with rejected inputs, exceptions, halts and oversized (larger than the rx buffer) inputs.
Inputs of 4 GiB or more in the README referee model (the machine API refuses lengths above uint32; the model sets no input size limit); not tested.
More than 2^24 input files given to the README referee model (prt.lua new_dapp_contract does not check the count).
Reorganization handling of the epoch listener and of crisium's get_seal, which reads the previous seal at the tip rather than through the input policy.
The Linux kernel cmio driver (out of scope) and how it validates the fromhost length.

rollup-http-server with real application HTTP clients (keep-alive and request timeouts under long input processing), the echo-dapp and rollup-http-client crates, the yield and hex tools, libcmt's mock io.
Portals and the other cartesi-rollups-contracts paths that add inputs on behalf of users; output validation contracts beyond LibMachineValidityProof.
Dave Tournament match and clock logic, bonds and refunds (claimant angle).
Provider-side limits on a single block's eth_getLogs response when a block is filled with maximum-size inputs (the log history raises on a failure for a single block and a single address).
The forked (in-memory) player of prt.lua under input floods, the machine cache replay cost per response, the frontier-forest storage code, and prt-demo.lua (harness).
